# Discovery scope

The source was exact PR5786. Canonical main was
`de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8.
The initial public overlap refresh covered 345 open PRs and 5175 Discussion
records with complete remote pagination. The sparse local inventory was
incomplete. Published and unpublished work can differ; a search is not a
certificate of novelty. A final full cached refresh stopped at an approval
timeout. A direct read then checked the 20 most recently updated PRs and
20 most recently updated Discussions. This later read was not a complete
remote snapshot.

The first tests extended the lifetime of an unchanged decoded value across
native MOVE operations. The fixed source had no repeated native output value
up to a nonzero scalar. A modular causal-span screen found no query output
in the span of earlier values in its destination frame. These are discovery
observations about that word, not universal exclusions.

The positive change uses the dual operation: collect several additions to an
unread destination, then convert their sum once. A finite graph-cut search
compared retained source copies with destination accumulation. Native costs
used the complete paid moment; helper boundary changes replaced their old
credits. The chosen construction needs no new source copy.

The discovery program used Python 3.12, PyMaxflow 1.3.2 and rounded integer
power costs. Those costs proposed candidates; they did not certify the final
price. The final plan has exact node IDs, event indices, coefficients and
source/output hashes. Its replay uses only the standard library and no optimizer.

Four provisional steps passed exact scalar replay. The largest touched role 92
and the contact region reserved in Discussion5125. PR5796 subsequently made
that block public. This contribution excludes the provisional role 92 step and
leaves its composition to the separate investigation. The search was rerun
with that region fixed. The accepted three steps use destinations 146,173,151.
The verifier also freezes the original R22 contact region. It compares 1704
protected events, their public boundary frames and all 23 exact COPY values.

Additional finite screens used the 1092 source frames,1313 subspaces derived
from neighboring sums and intersections, scalar-rescaling groups, both choices
of one moving helper endpoint,567 sampled linear transvections, and 1022 common
hyperplane-intersection or line-sum transformations. They did not add an
accepted gain. These discovery screens were not exhaustive over native charts,
scalar schedules, target contracts or multiple-frame plans. Their scratch
optimizers are not needed to reproduce this contribution, and no negative
theorem or global optimum is claimed from them.

The source-bound first command was `python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`.
The selected record was read directly and its main revision was checked. The
binding command stopped on omitted selected-source files in the sparse checkout;
it is not reported as a pass. No selected scientific replay was claimed.
The new package has its own complete authenticated source export and registered
verification. That export needs neither the omitted checkout files nor Git.

Credit PR5786, PR5774, PR5751, flyingviper's PR5718, Joel Pulikkan's R22 work,
the separate PR5795/5796 constructions, and all retained P104/native/controller/
compiler/BIT sources. The later transposed-supplier scope in
[Discussion5125](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5125#discussioncomment-19154639)
uses the same source/destination duality. That broader search is concurrent
work and remains separate from these three fixed forward-supplier steps.
The accumulation identity is elementary linearity. The
contribution is its legal placement, changed complete invoice and conditional
kappa result. Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No subagents.
